system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering JPMorgan Chase (JPM) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: UPDATE 1-JPMorgan profit falls on one-time Apple card deal charge

BODY:
(Adds details and context throughout)

Jan 13 (Reuters) - JPMorgan Chase's profit fell in the fourth quarter as it took a one-time charge tied to its agreement with Goldman Sachs to take over a credit card partnership with Apple.

Profit fell to $13 billion, or $4.63 per share, in the three months ended December 31, JPMorgan reported on Tuesday. That compares with $14 billion, or $4.81 per share, a year earlier.

Earlier this month, JPMorgan and Apple struck a deal under which the bank became the new issuer of the iPhone maker's card.

The deal would strengthen JPMorgan's foothold in credit cards and add to a long list of strategic wins for CEO Jamie Dimon, who has turned the bank into a leading player across retail and investment banking.

The bank had said it expects to record a $2.2 billion provision for credit losses in the fourth quarter tied to the portfolio.

The deal comes at a critical juncture for the credit card industry, which could face a sharp shift if a proposal by U.S. President Donald Trump to cap interest rates at 10% moves forward. While Trump has said he expects companies to comply by January 20, Wall Street analysts remain doubtful the measure can be implemented without congressional approval.

A banking industry body warned last week that the move could tighten access to credit for consumers and small businesses and drive borrowers toward unregulated lenders.

Excluding the one-time charge, JPMorgan's quarterly profit increased to $14.7 billion, or $5.23 per share, fueled by trading.

(Reporting by Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Saeed Azhar in New York, editing by Lananh Nguyen and Sriraj Kalluvila)
</article>

<summary>
JPMorgan's Q4 profit fell to $13 billion ($4.63 EPS) from $14 billion ($4.81 EPS) a year earlier, driven by a one-time $2.2 billion credit loss provision tied to its new Apple card partnership, taken over from Goldman Sachs. Excluding this charge, adjusted profit rose to $14.7 billion ($5.23 EPS), boosted by strong trading results. The Apple deal strengthens JPMorgan's credit card position under CEO Jamie Dimon but arrives amid regulatory uncertainty, as a proposed Trump administration cap on interest rates at 10% could disrupt the credit card industry, though implementation without Congressional approval remains doubtful.
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to JPM)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about JPM in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a JPM analyst what matters, and represent how central JPM really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for JPM, and says so plainly if JPM is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the JPM angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores JPM, or implies the article is about / important for JPM when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
